I guess there are a lot of ways how to study and everybody has their method. My method is somewhat good for me, but I wonder if there are any better methods.

My method consist of reading the first (introductory) paragraph and highlighting all the important keywords. Then reading the whole chapter while marking those words. This is my method which works 90% of the time:

I take note of the days which I will have an exam from our class syllabus. Then 2 weeks before the exam, I will start to study everything covered in the test. I will then divide the lessons into 13 parts and study a part of that lesson per day. That way I'll have a lot of time to prepare for it.

Only times that that didn't work is when a teacher decides to be a douche and completely fucks the course syllabus by announcing that the test will be move one week earlier which completely fucks my schedule.

I don't normally do a lot of studying, unless it is for a history class. I just pay attention in class and figure out patterns with the teacher (like if the teacher spends a lot of time on one problem and goes through every detail, strong chance it will be on the test, so I will take good notes and memorize the process).

Another thing I do is discuss things I learn with people. In high school I would discuss and debate history with my dad, so the things I already knew became further ingrained in me, and I learned things that my dad knew.

If the situation does occur there's an automatic and manual loop within the drone

If they're flying close to each other they'll send each other IFF signals to confirm whether the opposing drone. If it's friendly the drones can easily communicate and arrange new co-ordinates automatically. This is to reduce friendly fire incidents like the one you had just mentioned. If it's an enemy drone then it is a really difficult, it would depend mostly on the political climate which has led to varying incidents in the past. There are avenues for enemy drones to communicate with each other to prevent a mid air collision, however, usually the least powerful aircraft gives way to the opposing aircraft. A failure of finding a compromise can lead to a serious accident such as the "Hanain Island Incident" which killed one Chinese fighter and had injured one US pilot. There was the also drone incident over Georgia which caused the Russian MiG 25 to shoot the Georgian drone with anti air missiles.
